sourceRefs.locator: The Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia, ch. 7. In the section on negotiations after Rua’s death, Sinor identifies Plintha, the quaestor Epigenes and Hunnic representatives as the negotiators near Margus.
pp. 296–297 and n. 6. Priscus on the increase from 350 to 700 pounds and probable date 434. Discussion of fugitive claims in later agreements.
pp. 69–71, esp. nn. 107–114. Treaty of Margus dated to 435, conditions for Hunnic merchants, extradition of fugitives, and annual payment.
Opening topographical description and fig. 1. Margum near the confluence of the Morava and Danube at Orašje, Dubravica. Distinction from the fort opposite.
Peuce 8, p. 177 and n. 37. Compares the usual date of 435 with Constantin Zuckerman’s winter 439/440 based on the quaestorship of Epigenes.
